Build agents that run on your own computer

A local-first agent toolkit: a tool-using agent that needs no API key (a local model does the thinking), optional Claude as a stronger brain, and a council of persona agents with faces that deliberate together.

The layers

Analogy: a building. Each floor only uses the floors below it. You talk to the top floor (command line or GUI); the council floor runs meetings; the core floor is one agent's think-act loop; underneath, the brain (model backends) and the hands (tools) share one set of rules (messages, config, safety).

Every Python file starts with a [LAYER / name] label, and docs/FILE_MAP.md lists them all.

Quick start

How an agent works

Analogy: a chef with a recipe. Each step they either ask a kitchen hand (a tool) to fetch, chop or measure something, or plate the dish (the final answer). A step limit stops a chef who keeps asking forever.
  • Backend: the model. Local (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio) or Claude, with automatic fallback.
  • Tools: Python functions with a name, description and JSON schema. Arguments are validated before they run.
  • Safety: a workspace fence, approval prompts, a blocklist, a network guard, redacted logs.
  • Guards in the loop: never runs cut-off tool calls, stops repeated identical calls, rolls back on failure, and can be stopped.

Profile builder

Every tool's description is sent to the model on every request. Pick only what an agent needs, so its context window stays free for the actual work.

Analogy: send a plumber with a plumber's toolbox, not the whole hardware store.

Result

Tool descriptions as a share of the context window. Aim for under ~25% on local models.

Personas & faces

  
A persona is a council member with a name, role, personality, speaking style, and a procedurally drawn face
  drawn in plain ASCII text (about 2 KB per persona) with seven expressions. The GUI animates them live:
  eyes dart and thought dots grow while they deliberate, the mouth moves while they speak, and they blink when idle.

  

  
Make your own

  
Use the GUI's Personas tab (live face editor), or drop a JSON file in ./personas/:

  

  
Every face part comes from a fixed menu (hair, head shape, eyes, nose, mouth, glasses, beard, earrings, freckles, colour),
  so a hand-edited file can't inject anything into the page or terminal.



Safety centre

  
Defence in depth. Each layer catches what the one before misses, and fire drills prove they hold.

  

  
Fire drills
Run them with python -m hybrid_agent diagnose or the GUI's Safety tab. Each one simulates an attack or failure
  in a throwaway folder. Destructive commands are only ever checked, never executed, and tripwires block real network
  connections during drills.

  



Setup & models

  
Choosing a local model

  
Rule of thumb: about 0.6 GB of memory per billion parameters at 4-bit, plus room for context. For a council,
  different models (qwen + llama + mistral) disagree more usefully than three copies of one.
